newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African stock market closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.African stock market closing report.

text.p: South African shares powered ahead to finish Tuesday on a high following a better-than-expected U.S. CPI number and were further propelled by an early jump on Wall Street.
Dealers said that shares had been treading water awaiting the release of the U.S. data which would remove uncertainty from Wall Street and other markets.
"It is on the U.S. CPI. It was much, much better than expected and bodes very well in the short-term," said James Scott, dealer at Societe Generale Frankel Pollak.
"The figure has managed to allay many fears of another 25 basis point hike in U.S. interest rates," Scott said.
U.S. March Consumer Price inflation rose 0.1 percent compared to a 0.3 percent rise in February. Analysts had expected a 0.2 percent rise.

After Wall Street's 148-point plunge last Friday, local stocks have been anxiously waiting for the U.S. market to settle down. Many believed there would be a further correction on Wall Street and that Monday's firmer close could not be taken to seriously.
But dealers were saying late on Tuesday that things were starting to look much better for equities worldwide.
"The picture seems to have brightened up a bit. Things are looking quite good and we could see the industrials particularly move higher still," one dealer said.
Wall Street was last at 6,536.59 points, 84.69 points up.
Volumes for the day were fair to large, improving particularly when market uncertainty evaporated.
Gold shares continued to disappoint, dipping from the start of trade and shedding more in later as investors climbed into industrials, dragging the gold index to its lowest level in 17 months.
Industrials added 70.7 points to 8,237.5 points, all-shares climbed 30.9 points to 6,997.3 and golds lost 12.6 to 1,270.7.

News that Anglo American Platinum Corp of South Africa planned to merge its platinum companies and also build a big new platinum mine sent its companies' shares to a day's high on Tuesday, dealers said.

Shortly after the announcement Rustenburg Platinum Holdings Ltd climbed 100 cents to 72 rand with 121,500 shares changing hands and Potgietersrust Platinums Ltd rose 150 cents to 26.50 rand with 114,100 shares changing hands.
Amplats itself added 60 cents on the day to 29 rand in a volume of 221,100 shares.
Other features were Gencor which was off 20 cents to 19 rand, Sappi which climbed 150 cents to 35 rand and Sasol which was up 125 cents to 53.25 rand.

South African industrial equity futures firmed by late trade on Tuesday also on the back of the U.S. CPI figure and taking further heart from Wall Street. Despite dealers' earlier doubts, futures regained Monday's losses and more.
But gold contracts were weak and looked like falling further as bullion sank.
The June industrial contract was at 8,070/71 from 7,974, the all-share was at 6,475/85 from 6,425 and the gold futures contract was at 883/895 from 908.
-- Melanie Cheary, Johannesburg newsroom +27 11 482-1003
